the_signal.headline: MCP servers now plug directly into agents—70+ integrations live
the_signal.body: n8n's one-click MCP server connections eliminate friction between agent logic and external tools. For GTM engineers shipping agent-powered revenue systems, this cuts integration time from days to minutes—meaning faster iteration on customer-facing automation. When your comp is shipping agents faster, this becomes table stakes.

tool_drop.name: Mcptoon
tool_drop.what: Token-efficient MCP CLI client for local model inference
tool_drop.why: If you're building cost-conscious agent workflows that can't afford Claude API calls on every execution, this CLI reduces token overhead for local MCP operations—direct cost impact on your CAC math.

thread_of_day.title: Your AI project WILL break. Welcome to the Day 2 problem.
thread_of_day.takeaway: Most revenue teams build agents for Day 1 (demo/launch) but skip Day 2 questions (monitoring, failure modes, drift)—then watch them break in production when volumes spike or model behavior changes.

quote.text: The questions to ask BEFORE you start building, to make sure it keeps working.
quote.source: n8n Blog — Your AI project WILL break

whats_moving.context: 70 servers now directly available via OAuth in n8n signals MCP is shifting from protocol to platform—agents no longer need custom integrations
n8n publishing guides on tracing, evaluation, and cost tracking indicates observability is no longer optional—it's how you prevent agent drift from destroying your funnel
Separate post on agent identity management suggests enterprises are moving beyond stateless agents to delegated, auditable access—critical for compliance-heavy GTM workflows

act_on_this: Audit your current agent workflows for Day 2 failure points: add monitoring and cost tracking for your top 3 revenue-critical agent paths this week before volumes force a breakfix.
